correctness.rationale: The commutator matrix and Hilbert/HS decomposition are explicit. An α-Lipschitz logarithm estimate, the uniformly bounded mean square of split-sum logarithmic ratios, the summable lattice quadrature derivative bound, and the exact continuum change of variables prove an O(α²) error. The remaining one-dimensional integral has limit π²α/6 by the alternating Basel identity. Beta-integral bounds prove the density specialization. The standalone exact finite tests supplement, not replace, the infinite-dimensional proof.

value.rationale: The classical Hilbert matrix is a canonical borderline bounded but noncompact moment Hankel operator. Power damping tends strongly to the identity, yet its commutator has a singular √α Hilbert–Schmidt cusp. The theorem determines its sharp universal coefficient and proves stability under all moment tails O(j^{-1-δ}), equivalently Hölder changes away from the endpoint of the underlying density. This resolves a natural quantitative invariant and a nontrivial universality phenomenon not implied by basic boundedness or Schatten criteria.
